8 Best FullStory Session Replay Alternatives in 2026
Compare 8 FullStory Session Replay alternatives. Amplitude Free: 2M events and 10K replays on the same data as Analytics, experiments, and guides.

Frequently asked questions about FullStory Session Replay alternatives
FullStory remains a strong digital experience platform for Fullcapture session replay, frustration signals, and searchable UX investigation.
Teams still look elsewhere for transparent self-serve pricing, native feature flags or A/B testing, error tracking, deeper free product-analytics event volume, or an Analytics-first platform where replay shares identity and cohorts with experiments and guides.
The best FullStory Session Replay alternatives in 2026 are Amplitude, PostHog, Mixpanel, LogRocket, Microsoft Clarity, Heap, Contentsquare, and OpenReplay.
Amplitude is the pick when you want strong product analytics and session replay on the same behavioral data (shared identity, cohorts, metrics), with feature experimentation, feature management, heatmaps on Plus and above, and guides and surveys in the same workflow.
See also Amplitude vs FullStory and best session replay tools .
Amplitude: Analytics, session replay, guides, surveys, experiments, and feature flags on the same data. 2M events and 10K replays on Free plan
PostHog: Open source or self-host. 5K free recordings plus flags and error tracking
Mixpanel: Product analytics peer with Free replay. 1M events and 10K replays
LogRocket: Frontend debugging with console and network. Pay per sessions; unlimited errors and logs on paid
Microsoft Clarity: Unlimited free web recordings
Heap: Autocapture first, replay as add-on
Contentsquare: Enterprise DXA or Hotjar-style UX stack
OpenReplay: Privacy-first self-hosted replay

Frequently asked questions
FullStory is built around Fullcapture session data, searchable replay, and UX investigation. Those strengths are real for support, UX, and digital experience teams.
Fullcapture and searchable session replay: Autocapture-style behavioral data you can query without rewriting every event first.
Frustration and sentiment signals: Rage clicks, dead clicks, and related cues help UX and support triage faster.
FullstoryFree volume: 30,000 sessions per month, 12 months of analytics retention, up to 10 users, no credit card, per FullStory's plans page as of September 2026.
Heatmaps and page-flow tooling: Click, scroll, and journey views sit next to replay on plans.
Privacy-by-default masking: Configurable masking and enterprise compliance packaging.
Guides and Surveys add-on: FullStory offers a Guides and Surveys plan add-on, so insight-to-intervention is possible without a separate tour tool.
Product analytics on plans: Funnels, retention, and related charts ship next to replay. FullStory is more than a recorder.
Teams still evaluate alternatives for concrete reasons.
Paid FullStory plans are sales-led quotes that are hard to forecast next to public usage calculators.
Free usage leans into session volume, while product and growth teams often want higher free product-analytics event quotas plus session replay on the same identity and cohorts.
Native feature flags, A/B testing, and error tracking are not the core offer on FullStory's plans page, so buyers often add Statsig for experimentation and flags (or LaunchDarkly / Optimizely), keep Sentry for errors, or move to a platform that ships those products together.
Others want Analytics-first depth with experiments and guides on the same data, or an open-source / self-host path.
As of September 2026, FullStory offers FullstoryFree plus quote-based Business, Advanced, and Enterprise plans. FullstoryFree includes 30,000 sessions per month, 12 months of analytics retention, and up to 10 users. Paid plans are sales-led. Mobile, StoryAI, Guides and Surveys, and Multi-Org are common add-ons.
Worked free-tier comparison: FullstoryFree wins pure free session volume (30K vs Amplitude Free's 10K monthly session replays).
Amplitude Free wins free product analytics event volume (2M events per month) plus connected experiments and guides at limited volumes on the same data model.
If your buying committee needs a public self-serve calculator for paid growth, FullStory's quote path is a common reason teams shortlist alternatives.
Here are eight FullStory Session Replay alternatives compared on analytics-plus-replay depth, free quotas, mobile support, experimentation, and pricing transparency.
1. Amplitude: best for Analytics plus session replay on one data model
Amplitude is an AI analytics platform that puts product analytics and session replay on the same behavioral data, then connects heatmaps (Plus and above), feature experimentation, feature management, and guides and surveys without bolting on a separate recorder stack.
Shared identity, cohorts, and metrics mean a funnel drop opens into the sessions that explain it, then into an experiment or guide for the same cohort.
Best for: Product, growth, and engineering teams that want Analytics-first depth with session replay, experiments, flags, and guides on one model
Pricing: Event-volume platform plans as of September 2026.
Free: 2M events per month, 10K monthly session replays, 1-month replay retention, unlimited seats, no credit card; AI agents and Amplitude MCP on Free.
Plus starts at $0 (first 2M events free); heatmaps on Plus and above.
Growth includes 20K monthly replays; Enterprise includes 50K.
Growth and Enterprise through sales.
Details on Amplitude pricing .
Key features
Event-linked session replay. Open a replay from a chart, funnel, user look-up, or homepage. Web and mobile (Browser, iOS, Android, React Native) sync with the event stream, including rage clicks and dead clicks. See Amplitude Session Replay and the session replay docs .
Product analytics on the same data. Funnels, retention, cohort analysis, and trusted metrics share identity with replay.
Heatmaps on Plus and above. Page-level behavior sits next to product events and session replay per the pricing grid (not on Free).
Feature experimentation and feature management. Run flags and experiments against the same cohorts you filter in replay, instead of buying a separate flag or experiment vendor for the action step.
Guides and surveys. Launch a guide to the cohort you just watched, in the same workflow.
AI agents and Amplitude MCP on Free. Query behavioral context headlessly from tools like Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT; no separate AI usage add-on on Free per Amplitude pricing FAQs.
Pros: Twice Mixpanel Free's event volume (2M vs 1M) with the same 10K free monthly replay shape; closed loop from chart to replay to experiment to guide; mobile session replay shipping for web, iOS, Android, and React Native
Cons / less ideal if: Free and Plus cap monthly session replays at 10K with 1-month retention (FullstoryFree offers 30K sessions and longer analytics retention). Platform depth has a learning curve even though AI agents speed analysis and setup.
How Amplitude differs from FullStory: Leads with product analytics depth then connects session replay; public Free and Plus packaging with event plus replay quotas; native feature experimentation adjacency on Free at limited volumes; Free replay quota lower than FullstoryFree's 30K sessions
Where they're similar: Both ship session replay with frustration-oriented signals; both include product analytics and heatmaps on plans; both offer a path to in-app engagement (Amplitude guides and surveys; FullStory Guides and Surveys add-on)
Closest alternative: Mixpanel or PostHog
Try Amplitude for free today .
2. PostHog: best for engineering-led and self-hosted stacks
PostHog is an open-source product OS that bundles product analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, surveys, and error tracking. You can run PostHog Cloud or self-host when data residency is non-negotiable.
Best for: Engineers and technical founders who want flags, experiments, and errors next to replay
Pricing: Usage-based per product as of September 2026. Free monthly allowances include 1M events and 5K session recordings (resets monthly), plus free allowances for flags, experiments, surveys, and error tracking. Pay-as-you-go after free limits. Free recording retention is 1 month.
Key features: Session replay with console and network; feature flags and experiments in free allowances; error tracking next to the session; self-host under an open-source license
Pros: One SDK for analytics, replay, flags, and errors; self-host when policy requires it; public usage calculator
Cons / less ideal if: Free replay quota (5K) is lower than FullstoryFree (30K) and Amplitude Free (10K)
How PostHog differs from FullStory: Native flags, experiments, and error tracking; open-source and self-host path; lower free recording quota; engineering-first UX
Where they're similar: Both include session replay and product analytics; both help investigate UX and product issues from recordings
Closest alternative: OpenReplay or Amplitude
3. Mixpanel: best analytics peer with Free replay quotas
Mixpanel is a product analytics suite with session replay on Free, Growth, and Enterprise for web, iOS, Android, and React Native. It is the closest peer when you want event-based analytics plus free replay without a DXA-first vendor.
Best for: Product and growth teams that want Mixpanel-shaped analytics with 10K free monthly replays
Pricing: As of September 2026. Free: 1M events per month, 10K session replays per month, unlimited seats. Growth from $0 (first 1M events free); Enterprise custom. Experiments and feature flags on Free and Growth with volume limits, per Mixpanel's pricing page.
Key features: Web and mobile session replay (iOS, Android, React Native); heatmaps and AI summaries; rage and dead clicks; experiments and feature flags on Free and Growth (volume-limited)
Pros: Clear Free and Growth calculator; same 10K free replay shape as Amplitude; experiments and flags without a second vendor
Cons / less ideal if: Free events are 1M vs Amplitude's 2M; thinner guides packaging than Amplitude
How Mixpanel differs from FullStory: Event-volume free analytics (1M); public Growth calculator; experiments and flags on Free and Growth; lower free session volume than FullstoryFree (10K vs 30K)
Where they're similar: Both ship session replay with product analytics adjacency; both support mobile session replay (FullStory often via Mobile add-on on paid)
Closest alternative: Amplitude
4. LogRocket: best for production frontend debugging
LogRocket is a session replay, product analytics, and error monitoring suite aimed at engineering teams. You pay for sessions captured while analytics events, errors, and logs stay unlimited on paid packages.
Best for: Frontend engineers and QA debugging production UI failures with console and network context
Pricing: Pay per sessions captured as of September 2026. Public calculator example around $176/mo at 25K sessions (final price depends on seats, retention, and add-ons). A free tier is not clearly listed on LogRocket's primary pricing page as of September 2026; treat third-party "1K free" claims as unverified.
Key features: Replay plus console, network, and state; unlimited analytics and errors on paid plans; Galileo AI on Pro and above; conditional recording rules
Pros: Debug depth DXA-first tools rarely match; predictable when error volume spikes
Cons / less ideal if: Less PM analytics depth than Amplitude or Mixpanel; no clear Free analytics-plus-replay plan on the primary pricing page
How LogRocket differs from FullStory: Engineering debug as the center of gravity; session-based public calculator; error monitoring is first-class
Where they're similar: Both center high-fidelity session replay for issue investigation; both pair replay with supporting analytics
Closest alternative: PostHog or OpenReplay
5. Microsoft Clarity: best for unlimited free web recordings
Microsoft Clarity is a free session recording and heatmap product. It is a recorder and visualization layer, not a product analytics or experimentation platform. Many teams run it beside Amplitude or Mixpanel for qualitative web replay without another invoice.
Best for: Marketers, growth, and UX folks who need zero-cost web recordings next to an existing analytics stack
Pricing: Free forever as of September 2026. Unlimited recordings and heatmaps per Microsoft's marketing claim. No paid Clarity plan.
Key features: Unlimited recordings and heatmaps; AI summaries and rage or dead click detection; mobile app SDKs claimed (Android, iOS, Flutter, React Native); still need a separate tool for funnels, experiments, and guides
Pros: Zero cost; fast heatmap and rage-click scans; easy stack pairing
Cons / less ideal if: You want to replace FullStory Session Replay and product analytics in one move
How Microsoft Clarity differs from FullStory: Free forever for basic web replay; no FullStory-depth DXA analytics; usually a complement, not a replacement
Where they're similar: Both offer session recordings and heatmaps; both surface frustration cues
Closest alternative: Contentsquare Free or FullstoryFree
6. Heap: best for autocapture with session replay as an add-on
Heap is an autocapture product analytics platform, now part of Contentsquare. Session replay arrives through the Experience Analytics add-on on Pro and Premier, not on Free or Growth core.
Best for: Product and growth teams that want autocapture first and can budget Pro or Premier plus Experience Analytics for replay
Pricing: Session-based as of September 2026. Free: up to 10K monthly sessions, core analytics, 6 months history. Growth estimate in-product; Pro and Premier custom. Session replay is the Experience Analytics add-on on Pro and Premier only.
Key features: Autocapture and retroactive analysis; Free tier up to 10K monthly sessions; Experience Analytics add-on (session replay, Error Analysis, heatmaps) on Pro and Premier only
Pros: Autocapture without a full tracking-plan rewrite; retroactive event definitions; Contentsquare adjacency
Cons / less ideal if: You need FullStory-style replay on day one without a Pro or Premier plus add-on deal
How Heap differs from FullStory: Autocapture analytics first; replay gated behind a paid add-on; Free tier is analytics sessions, not FullstoryFree-style replay volume
Where they're similar: Both help investigate digital experience issues; both sit in the broader DXA / product analytics category
Closest alternative: Contentsquare or Amplitude
7. Contentsquare: best for enterprise DXA and the Hotjar successor path
Contentsquare is an experience intelligence platform spanning Experience Analytics (session replay, heatmaps, journeys) and related lines. Hotjar pricing for new buyers now routes into Contentsquare packaging. Legacy Hotjar Observe or Plus self-serve prices are not the live new-customer offer.
Best for: Marketing-site and enterprise DXA teams that want Hotjar-style UX tooling at Contentsquare scale
Pricing: Modular Free / Growth / Pro / Enterprise as of September 2026.
Contentsquare Free includes session replay and heatmaps; Contentsquare's blog states up to 200,000 monthly sessions on Free.
Growth is self-serve; published third parties have cited roughly $49/mo entry ([VERIFY] against contentsquare.com/pricing before treating dollars as final).
Pro and Enterprise are sales-led.
Key features: Experience Analytics (replay, heatmaps, journeys); high Free session ceiling per Contentsquare's free-plan blog; Hotjar brand path into Contentsquare packaging; enterprise DXA breadth
Pros: High free session volume; Hotjar-to-Contentsquare continuity; enterprise DXA tooling
Cons / less ideal if: You need Amplitude- or Mixpanel-depth product analytics, experiments, and flags on a public Free event quota
How Contentsquare differs from FullStory: Broader experience intelligence portfolio and Hotjar brand path; very high Free session ceiling per Contentsquare blog; modular Free / Growth / Pro / Enterprise packaging
Where they're similar: Both are DXA-class platforms with session replay and heatmaps; both serve enterprise digital experience teams
Closest alternative: FullStory itself (if DXA-first is the job) or Microsoft Clarity
8. OpenReplay: best for privacy-first self-hosted replay
OpenReplay is an open-source session replay platform with developer tools, co-browsing, and product analytics options. Self-host is free. Dedicated managed cloud starts at $199/mo.
Best for: Engineering and security-conscious teams that must keep session data on their own infrastructure
Pricing: Open-source self-host free (you run the infrastructure). Dedicated from $199/mo as of September 2026; Enterprise custom for large self-host deployments.
Key features: Open-source self-host; developer tools (network and console); Dedicated from $199/mo with SSO and custom retention; strong on replay and privacy, thinner as a FullStory-depth DXA suite alone
Pros: Data residency control; developer tooling without a SaaS recorder mandate; clear Dedicated entry price
Cons / less ideal if: You want a managed FullStory- or Amplitude-like analytics and experimentation suite without operating a replay cluster
How OpenReplay differs from FullStory: Self-host and open-source first; public Dedicated price floor ($199/mo); developer tools emphasis closer to LogRocket
Where they're similar: Both focus on high-quality session replay for issue investigation; both offer paths to product analytics alongside recordings
Closest alternative: PostHog or LogRocket

Match the constraint that actually blocks you.
Need analytics, session replay, guides, surveys, experiments, and feature flags on one data set, plus 2M free events and 10K free replays? Amplitude is the most complete alternative. You give up FullstoryFree's 30K session volume.
Need open-source or self-host with flags, experiments, and error tracking? PostHog fits. You give up FullStory's higher free session volume.
Need a product analytics peer with Free replay and a public Growth calculator? Mixpanel fits. You give up Amplitude's higher free event volume.
Need console and network next to every recording? LogRocket fits. You give up a clear Free analytics-plus-replay plan.
Need unlimited free web recordings beside analytics you already trust? Microsoft Clarity fits. You give up replacing FullStory in one move.
Need autocapture first and can buy replay later? Heap fits. You give up session replay on Free and Growth.
Need enterprise DXA or the current Hotjar buyer path? Contentsquare fits. You give up Amplitude-style free event quotas.
Need recordings on your own infrastructure? OpenReplay fits. You give up a managed FullStory-like DXA suite unless you add more tools.
Need the next step after a replay to be an in-app guide? Consider Pendo (honorable mention): strong guides loop; sales-led packaging with an unlimited replays claim.
Decide on budget, hosting, or platform breadth first, then dual-run two SDKs for a sprint. Related: Mixpanel Session Replay alternatives , PostHog Session Replay alternatives , Hotjar alternatives .
Dual-run SDKs. Keep FullStory capturing while you install Amplitude Browser, iOS, Android, or React Native SDKs and session replay plugins.
Map events and cohorts. Port the funnels, segments, and frustration definitions your team actually uses. Historical event export is often possible; session recordings are generally not portable across vendors because formats are proprietary.
Match privacy masking. Rebuild masking, blocklists, and consent behavior so Amplitude capture meets the same bar as FullStory before you cut traffic over.
Validate for one or two sprints. Compare funnel counts, replay coverage, and mobile capture quality side by side, then ramp sampling.
Start from the docs. Use the session replay docs and Amplitude vs FullStory for the head-to-head feature map.
Public Amplitude customer stories on the Session Replay product page (for example Evaneos, EA, and TourRadar) illustrate why teams pair qualitative replay with funnel analysis after a drop. Re-verify any quoted lift figures on amplitude.com before citing them in downstream collateral.
We're biased, so here's the short version.
Amplitude is a strong fit if you:
Want product analytics and session replay sharing identity, cohorts, and metrics with feature experimentation, feature management, heatmaps (Plus and above), and guides and surveys in one workflow
Prefer a Free plan with 2M events a month and 10K session replays before you talk to sales
Are consolidating a FullStory-plus-analytics or FullStory-plus-flags stack into one system of record from chart to replay to experiment to guide
If that matches how your team works, Try Amplitude for free today . Details live on Amplitude pricing and Amplitude Session Replay . For a pure head-to-head, see Amplitude vs FullStory . For the broader category, see best session replay tools and best product analytics tools .
Try Amplitude for free today to see how Analytics, session replay, experimentation, and guides work on one data model.
What are the best FullStory Session Replay alternatives in 2026?
Amplitude, PostHog, Mixpanel, LogRocket, Microsoft Clarity, Heap, Contentsquare, and OpenReplay.
Amplitude leads for product analytics and session replay on the same data model with experiments and guides.
PostHog fits self-hosted stacks.
Mixpanel is the closest analytics peer.
The rest cover debug depth, zero-cost web replay, autocapture, enterprise DXA, and self-hosted privacy.
Is FullStory free?
Yes. FullstoryFree includes 30,000 sessions per month, 12 months of analytics retention, and up to 10 users with no credit card, per FullStory's plans page as of September 2026. Business, Advanced, and Enterprise are quote-based; Mobile, StoryAI, and Guides and Surveys are common add-ons.
Does FullStory have feature flags or A/B testing?
Native feature flags and A/B testing are not offered as core products on FullStory's plans page as of September 2026. Buyers typically add Statsig for experimentation and flags (or LaunchDarkly / Optimizely), or a platform like PostHog, Amplitude, or Mixpanel. Re-check FullStory plans before treating that gap as permanent.
Does FullStory have error tracking?
FullStory surfaces error-related frustration signals in the DXA workflow, but dedicated Sentry-style exception tracking is not the core offer on the plans page. Engineering teams often keep a separate error tool or pick PostHog or LogRocket.
FullStory vs Amplitude: which is better for session replay?
FullStory leads on Fullcapture UX maturity and FullstoryFree session volume (30K). Amplitude leads when session replay must share identity, cohorts, and metrics with product analytics, feature experimentation, and guides and surveys (Free: 2M events and 10K replays). See Amplitude vs FullStory .
What is the best free alternative to FullStory?
For free product analytics plus replay, Amplitude Free (2M events and 10K replays). For free session volume alone, FullstoryFree (30K), Contentsquare Free (up to ~200K sessions per Contentsquare's blog), or Microsoft Clarity (unlimited web).
PostHog or Amplitude for replacing FullStory?
Choose Amplitude if PMs need Analytics-first depth, shared cohorts with experiments and guides, and a 2M-event Free plan. Choose PostHog if engineers need self-hosting, error tracking, and an open-source stack, and can accept a 5K free recording limit.
How do I migrate from FullStory to Amplitude?
Dual-run SDKs, map critical events and cohorts, enable Amplitude Browser, iOS, Android, or React Native session replay plugins, match privacy masking, and validate for one or two sprints. Recordings generally are not portable. Start from the session replay docs .
Does FullStory support mobile session replay?
Yes, on paid packaging. FullStory's plans page lists Mobile as an add-on. Do not assume FullstoryFree includes native mobile capture. Amplitude documents web plus iOS, Android, and React Native session replay.
FullStory vs LogRocket: which is better for debugging?
LogRocket is stronger when console, network, and state must sit on the same timeline as the recording. FullStory is stronger for UX frustration analysis and DXA workflows.
What happened to Hotjar and Smartlook if I was comparing them to FullStory?
Hotjar pricing for new buyers routes into Contentsquare packaging; do not use legacy Hotjar Observe or Plus dollar figures as current. Smartlook is winding down (decommissioning through September 30, 2027) and is not recommended here.
Session replay vs product analytics: do I need both?
Often yes. Product analytics tells you which cohort dropped; session replay shows what those users saw. Platforms that share identity across both (Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog) reduce tool-switching. DXA-first tools still include analytics layers; depth of retention and experiment workflows is the real question.

Heatmaps on Plus and above. Page-level behavior sits next to product events and session replay per the pricing grid (not on Free).
Feature experimentation and feature management. Run flags and experiments against the same cohorts you filter in replay, instead of buying a separate flag or experiment vendor for the action step.
Guides and surveys. Launch a guide to the cohort you just watched, in the same workflow.
AI agents and Amplitude MCP on Free. Query behavioral context headlessly from tools like Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT; no separate AI usage add-on on Free per Amplitude pricing FAQs.

Pros: Twice Mixpanel Free's event volume (2M vs 1M) with the same 10K free monthly replay shape; closed loop from chart to replay to experiment to guide; mobile session replay shipping for web, iOS, Android, and React Native

Cons / less ideal if: Free and Plus cap monthly session replays at 10K with 1-month retention (FullstoryFree offers 30K sessions and longer analytics retention). Platform depth has a learning curve even though AI agents speed analysis and setup.

How Amplitude differs from FullStory: Leads with product analytics depth then connects session replay; public Free and Plus packaging with event plus replay quotas; native feature experimentation adjacency on Free at limited volumes; Free replay quota lower than FullstoryFree's 30K sessions

Where they're similar: Both ship session replay with frustration-oriented signals; both include product analytics and heatmaps on plans; both offer a path to in-app engagement (Amplitude guides and surveys; FullStory Guides and Surveys add-on)
Closest alternative: Mixpanel or PostHog
Try Amplitude for free today .
2. PostHog: best for engineering-led and self-hosted stacks

PostHog is an open-source product OS that bundles product analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, surveys, and error tracking. You can run PostHog Cloud or self-host when data residency is non-negotiable.
Best for: Engineers and technical founders who want flags, experiments, and errors next to replay

Pricing: Usage-based per product as of September 2026. Free monthly allowances include 1M events and 5K session recordings (resets monthly), plus free allowances for flags, experiments, surveys, and error tracking. Pay-as-you-go after free limits. Free recording retention is 1 month.
Key features: Session replay with console and network; feature flags and experiments in free allowances; error tracking next to the session; self-host under an open-source license
Pros: One SDK for analytics, replay, flags, and errors; self-host when policy requires it; public usage calculator
Cons / less ideal if: Free replay quota (5K) is lower than FullstoryFree (30K) and Amplitude Free (10K)
How PostHog differs from FullStory: Native flags, experiments, and error tracking; open-source and self-host path; lower free recording quota; engineering-first UX
Where they're similar: Both include session replay and product analytics; both help investigate UX and product issues from recordings
Closest alternative: OpenReplay or Amplitude
3. Mixpanel: best analytics peer with Free replay quotas

Mixpanel is a product analytics suite with session replay on Free, Growth, and Enterprise for web, iOS, Android, and React Native. It is the closest peer when you want event-based analytics plus free replay without a DXA-first vendor.
Best for: Product and growth teams that want Mixpanel-shaped analytics with 10K free monthly replays

Pricing: As of September 2026. Free: 1M events per month, 10K session replays per month, unlimited seats. Growth from $0 (first 1M events free); Enterprise custom. Experiments and feature flags on Free and Growth with volume limits, per Mixpanel's pricing page.
Key features: Web and mobile session replay (iOS, Android, React Native); heatmaps and AI summaries; rage and dead clicks; experiments and feature flags on Free and Growth (volume-limited)
Pros: Clear Free and Growth calculator; same 10K free replay shape as Amplitude; experiments and flags without a second vendor
Cons / less ideal if: Free events are 1M vs Amplitude's 2M; thinner guides packaging than Amplitude
How Mixpanel differs from FullStory: Event-volume free analytics (1M); public Growth calculator; experiments and flags on Free and Growth; lower free session volume than FullstoryFree (10K vs 30K)
Where they're similar: Both ship session replay with product analytics adjacency; both support mobile session replay (FullStory often via Mobile add-on on paid)
Closest alternative: Amplitude
4. LogRocket: best for production frontend debugging

LogRocket is a session replay, product analytics, and error monitoring suite aimed at engineering teams. You pay for sessions captured while analytics events, errors, and logs stay unlimited on paid packages.
Best for: Frontend engineers and QA debugging production UI failures with console and network context

Pricing: Pay per sessions captured as of September 2026. Public calculator example around $176/mo at 25K sessions (final price depends on seats, retention, and add-ons). A free tier is not clearly listed on LogRocket's primary pricing page as of September 2026; treat third-party "1K free" claims as unverified.
Key features: Replay plus console, network, and state; unlimited analytics and errors on paid plans; Galileo AI on Pro and above; conditional recording rules
Pros: Debug depth DXA-first tools rarely match; predictable when error volume spikes
Cons / less ideal if: Less PM analytics depth than Amplitude or Mixpanel; no clear Free analytics-plus-replay plan on the primary pricing page
How LogRocket differs from FullStory: Engineering debug as the center of gravity; session-based public calculator; error monitoring is first-class
Where they're similar: Both center high-fidelity session replay for issue investigation; both pair replay with supporting analytics
Closest alternative: PostHog or OpenReplay
5. Microsoft Clarity: best for unlimited free web recordings

Microsoft Clarity is a free session recording and heatmap product. It is a recorder and visualization layer, not a product analytics or experimentation platform. Many teams run it beside Amplitude or Mixpanel for qualitative web replay without another invoice.
Best for: Marketers, growth, and UX folks who need zero-cost web recordings next to an existing analytics stack
Pricing: Free forever as of September 2026. Unlimited recordings and heatmaps per Microsoft's marketing claim. No paid Clarity plan.

Key features: Unlimited recordings and heatmaps; AI summaries and rage or dead click detection; mobile app SDKs claimed (Android, iOS, Flutter, React Native); still need a separate tool for funnels, experiments, and guides
Pros: Zero cost; fast heatmap and rage-click scans; easy stack pairing
Cons / less ideal if: You want to replace FullStory Session Replay and product analytics in one move
How Microsoft Clarity differs from FullStory: Free forever for basic web replay; no FullStory-depth DXA analytics; usually a complement, not a replacement
Where they're similar: Both offer session recordings and heatmaps; both surface frustration cues
Closest alternative: Contentsquare Free or FullstoryFree
6. Heap: best for autocapture with session replay as an add-on
Heap is an autocapture product analytics platform, now part of Contentsquare. Session replay arrives through the Experience Analytics add-on on Pro and Premier, not on Free or Growth core.
Best for: Product and growth teams that want autocapture first and can budget Pro or Premier plus Experience Analytics for replay

Pricing: Session-based as of September 2026. Free: up to 10K monthly sessions, core analytics, 6 months history. Growth estimate in-product; Pro and Premier custom. Session replay is the Experience Analytics add-on on Pro and Premier only.
Key features: Autocapture and retroactive analysis; Free tier up to 10K monthly sessions; Experience Analytics add-on (session replay, Error Analysis, heatmaps) on Pro and Premier only
Pros: Autocapture without a full tracking-plan rewrite; retroactive event definitions; Contentsquare adjacency
Cons / less ideal if: You need FullStory-style replay on day one without a Pro or Premier plus add-on deal
How Heap differs from FullStory: Autocapture analytics first; replay gated behind a paid add-on; Free tier is analytics sessions, not FullstoryFree-style replay volume
Where they're similar: Both help investigate digital experience issues; both sit in the broader DXA / product analytics category
Closest alternative: Contentsquare or Amplitude
7. Contentsquare: best for enterprise DXA and the Hotjar successor path

Contentsquare is an experience intelligence platform spanning Experience Analytics (session replay, heatmaps, journeys) and related lines. Hotjar pricing for new buyers now routes into Contentsquare packaging. Legacy Hotjar Observe or Plus self-serve prices are not the live new-customer offer.
Best for: Marketing-site and enterprise DXA teams that want Hotjar-style UX tooling at Contentsquare scale
Pricing: Modular Free / Growth / Pro / Enterprise as of September 2026.
Contentsquare Free includes session replay and heatmaps; Contentsquare's blog states up to 200,000 monthly sessions on Free.
Growth is self-serve; published third parties have cited roughly $49/mo entry ([VERIFY] against contentsquare.com/pricing before treating dollars as final).
Pro and Enterprise are sales-led.
Key features: Experience Analytics (replay, heatmaps, journeys); high Free session ceiling per Contentsquare's free-plan blog; Hotjar brand path into Contentsquare packaging; enterprise DXA breadth
Pros: High free session volume; Hotjar-to-Contentsquare continuity; enterprise DXA tooling
Cons / less ideal if: You need Amplitude- or Mixpanel-depth product analytics, experiments, and flags on a public Free event quota

How Contentsquare differs from FullStory: Broader experience intelligence portfolio and Hotjar brand path; very high Free session ceiling per Contentsquare blog; modular Free / Growth / Pro / Enterprise packaging
Where they're similar: Both are DXA-class platforms with session replay and heatmaps; both serve enterprise digital experience teams
Closest alternative: FullStory itself (if DXA-first is the job) or Microsoft Clarity
8. OpenReplay: best for privacy-first self-hosted replay
OpenReplay is an open-source session replay platform with developer tools, co-browsing, and product analytics options. Self-host is free. Dedicated managed cloud starts at $199/mo.
Best for: Engineering and security-conscious teams that must keep session data on their own infrastructure
Pricing: Open-source self-host free (you run the infrastructure). Dedicated from $199/mo as of September 2026; Enterprise custom for large self-host deployments.

Key features: Open-source self-host; developer tools (network and console); Dedicated from $199/mo with SSO and custom retention; strong on replay and privacy, thinner as a FullStory-depth DXA suite alone
Pros: Data residency control; developer tooling without a SaaS recorder mandate; clear Dedicated entry price
Cons / less ideal if: You want a managed FullStory- or Amplitude-like analytics and experimentation suite without operating a replay cluster
How OpenReplay differs from FullStory: Self-host and open-source first; public Dedicated price floor ($199/mo); developer tools emphasis closer to LogRocket
Where they're similar: Both focus on high-quality session replay for issue investigation; both offer paths to product analytics alongside recordings
Closest alternative: PostHog or LogRocket

What are the best FullStory Session Replay alternatives in 2026?
Amplitude, PostHog, Mixpanel, LogRocket, Microsoft Clarity, Heap, Contentsquare, and OpenReplay.
Amplitude leads for product analytics and session replay on the same data model with experiments and guides.
PostHog fits self-hosted stacks.
Mixpanel is the closest analytics peer.
The rest cover debug depth, zero-cost web replay, autocapture, enterprise DXA, and self-hosted privacy.
Is FullStory free?

Yes. FullstoryFree includes 30,000 sessions per month, 12 months of analytics retention, and up to 10 users with no credit card, per FullStory's plans page as of September 2026. Business, Advanced, and Enterprise are quote-based; Mobile, StoryAI, and Guides and Surveys are common add-ons.
Does FullStory have feature flags or A/B testing?

Native feature flags and A/B testing are not offered as core products on FullStory's plans page as of September 2026. Buyers typically add Statsig for experimentation and flags (or LaunchDarkly / Optimizely), or a platform like PostHog, Amplitude, or Mixpanel. Re-check FullStory plans before treating that gap as permanent.
Does FullStory have error tracking?

FullStory surfaces error-related frustration signals in the DXA workflow, but dedicated Sentry-style exception tracking is not the core offer on the plans page. Engineering teams often keep a separate error tool or pick PostHog or LogRocket.
FullStory vs Amplitude: which is better for session replay?

FullStory leads on Fullcapture UX maturity and FullstoryFree session volume (30K). Amplitude leads when session replay must share identity, cohorts, and metrics with product analytics, feature experimentation, and guides and surveys (Free: 2M events and 10K replays). See Amplitude vs FullStory .
What is the best free alternative to FullStory?

For free product analytics plus replay, Amplitude Free (2M events and 10K replays). For free session volume alone, FullstoryFree (30K), Contentsquare Free (up to ~200K sessions per Contentsquare's blog), or Microsoft Clarity (unlimited web).
PostHog or Amplitude for replacing FullStory?

Choose Amplitude if PMs need Analytics-first depth, shared cohorts with experiments and guides, and a 2M-event Free plan. Choose PostHog if engineers need self-hosting, error tracking, and an open-source stack, and can accept a 5K free recording limit.
How do I migrate from FullStory to Amplitude?

Dual-run SDKs, map critical events and cohorts, enable Amplitude Browser, iOS, Android, or React Native session replay plugins, match privacy masking, and validate for one or two sprints. Recordings generally are not portable. Start from the session replay docs .
Does FullStory support mobile session replay?

Yes, on paid packaging. FullStory's plans page lists Mobile as an add-on. Do not assume FullstoryFree includes native mobile capture. Amplitude documents web plus iOS, Android, and React Native session replay.
FullStory vs LogRocket: which is better for debugging?
LogRocket is stronger when console, network, and state must sit on the same timeline as the recording. FullStory is stronger for UX frustration analysis and DXA workflows.
What happened to Hotjar and Smartlook if I was comparing them to FullStory?

Hotjar pricing for new buyers routes into Contentsquare packaging; do not use legacy Hotjar Observe or Plus dollar figures as current. Smartlook is winding down (decommissioning through September 30, 2027) and is not recommended here.
Session replay vs product analytics: do I need both?

Often yes. Product analytics tells you which cohort dropped; session replay shows what those users saw. Platforms that share identity across both (Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog) reduce tool-switching. DXA-first tools still include analytics layers; depth of retention and experiment workflows is the real question.
